The SI unit of heat capacity is the joule per kelvin — this is correct.

The other two statements are not true: "A substance with a high specific heat capacity heats up very quickly" and "Specific heat capacity is measured in joules per kelvin" both misstate the physics.

So only I is correct.

text: 6400J of heat is supplied to 0.5kg of a substance of specific heat capacity 400J/kg·K. Calculate the rise in temperature.
explanation:
\(\Delta\theta = \frac{Q}{mc}\)

\(= \frac{6400}{0.5 \times 400} = 32\)K

text: 5400J of heat raises the temperature of 0.5kg of a substance by 12K. Calculate its specific heat capacity.
explanation:
\(c = \frac{Q}{m\Delta\theta}\)
